original_card.question: Can one specified masked or overcomplete decoder improve the complete moment budget?
methods: Synthesize a decoder with exact coefficients and fully priced helper endpoints.
Bound the best possible budget for a fixed support alphabet before synthesis.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound and count all copied information, frames and restoration.

first_step.inspect: Locate the excluded classes: masked identities, at least nine terms, and deeper punctures.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one finite support alphabet and test exact decoding constraints before building a whole network.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A cheaper fully realized decoder could increase deficit or lower recursive cost on the binding complex side.
allowed_variations: Select a specific masked or overcomplete family with exact labels and supports.
scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: On P112, what is the exact maximum of (E-graph 8-cliques hit) / (1260 * pairing rank) over port supports cut out by an F2^9 subspace of dimension at least 6?
scope_change_reason: The card's first experiment asks for one finite support alphabet and an exact decoding constraint before a network is built. The alphabet is the codimension-at-most-3 E-graph kernels from PR717 D1(e), an excluded masked class of the eight-term all-pairs theorem. The exhaustive frame ratio replaces that note's 20000-pair sample. Restoration beyond this frame quotient is not priced.
bottleneck_link: The complex side binds. A masked decoder cheaper than the eight-term floor would have to beat this frame-substitution quotient on the E-graph. The exact quotient 17/35 still leaves the covering relaxation at 280/17, below 64, so this alphabet does not by itself raise the complex budget.
stop_rule: Stop after the codimension-at-most-3 flat census and its witness check. Do not search proper subsets or build a supplier.
evidence: Witness hits 612 at beta 1, ratio 17/35, covering bound 280/17. Census command prints PASS_CENSUS 17/35. The sampled ratio 23/126 is strictly smaller. No kappa change. Discussion writes are forbidden for this account and were not retried.
author: AI-assisted research session
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance was used for the census, the independent witness check, and the packaging. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can a proper subset of one codimension-at-most-3 kernel raise the frame-hit ratio above 17/35?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A higher ratio would lower the covering bound 280/17 further. The flat census does not decide subsets, and a subset of a higher-rank kernel can drop beta faster than it drops the clique count.
open_questions.first_step: For each dimension-6 kernel whose self-pairing rank is at least 4, delete one port and recompute hits and beta. Keep a subset only if its ratio exceeds 17/35.
open_questions.blocked_by: The deletion family is outside the D1(e) flat list, and the deletion tree is larger than the flat census completed here.
